Farmers call it “a perfect storm of ugly.” 

Tariffs. Rising input costs. Cuts to rural health care. These headwinds are real, but they're not an excuse. 

If elected governor, I will find common ground and deliver real results for Greater Minnesota.

Today at the Nelson family farm outside Moorhead, my running mate Ben Schierer and I unveiled our plan to expand Minnesota's rural and agricultural economy.

The farm has been in the Nelson family for four generations and we need to keep it that way. Their 100-year-old grandma Dorothy was there and agrees!

posts.text:
Kids who grow up in rural Minnesota should be able to stay in rural Minnesota. 

That’s why today, at a farm outside Moorhead, Ben and I released our plan to expand Minnesota’s rural and agricultural economy and make sure that people are able to live, work, and raise a family in rural Minnesota.

Learn more: amyklobuchar.com/rural
posts.summary: Commits to rural economic expansion enabling people to live and work in rural Minnesota

As we innovate, our workforce must too. Dr. Behfar, a Mayo Clinic surgeon and biotech company founder, sees the need firsthand.

That's why we'll connect K-12, trades, and colleges to expand workforce pathways and develop the talent Minnesota needs right here at home.

Minnesota has 11,600 registered apprentices. I want to add 10,000 more — working with businesses and trade unions to expand apprenticeships into biotech, health care, manufacturing, and agriculture. It’s already happening in Rochester. Let’s expand it across the state.

posts.text:
When I’m Governor, we’ll ban cell phones and other mobile devices in all K–12 classrooms and work with school districts to set screen-time limits. We’ll bring proven curricula to Minnesota — phonics-based reading and quality math instruction. Because Minnesota's kids deserve nothing but the best.

Video

As Governor, I’ll make sure Minnesotans have the skills to build a good life here at home with 10,000 more apprenticeships and more.
